newsitem.title: USA: Unisys says on track for full-year profit.
newsitem.headline: Unisys says on track for full-year profit.

text.p: Unisys Corp said Monday it is on track toward its goal of delivering quarterly, year-over-year financial progress and full-year profitability in 1997.

"We are on track toward our goals of delivering quarterly, year-over-year financial progress and full-year profitability in 1997," said James Unruh, the company's chairman and chief executive officer, said,

The company reported a loss per share of $0.06 for the first quarter ended March 31 versus a loss of $0.25 for the same quarter a year ago. Analyst consensus for the quarter was a loss of $0.14, according to First Call.
Unruh said that the company grew its revenue while significantly improving its profitability and operating cash flow from a year ago.
Unisys said that revenue increased across all three business units.

Unisys said it's focused structure is improving the ability of its three units to capture opportunities in their respective markets, while also allowing it to offer its customers an integrated source of solutions.
Unisys said its results were driven by strong results from its Computer Systems business and another solid performance from its Global Customer Services unit.

Unisys said the Information Services Group continues to make progress in operational execution and in refining its business. Orders rose substantially in the quarter and the company continues to plan for this business to achieve operating profitability on a run-rate basis by year-end 1997.
However, operational issues associated with a few large, multi-year contracts negatively affected the unit's profitability in the quarter by approximately $25 million.

Revenue for the quarter increased eight percent to $1.53 billion from $1.42 billion a year ago, despite the negative impact of currency. Orders were similar to year-ago levels. Orders increased in the United States while international orders declined, principally due to the impact of currency and the timing of a few large orders in the year-ago period.

Unisys said its cash balance fell by about $340 million to approximately $700 million in the quarter. The reduction primarily reflects the redemption of $100 million preferred stock by Mitsui & Co. and management's decision to reduce the level of accounts receivable factoring by about $140 million.
